title: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents
author: Tianle Chen, Pushkar Singh, Ketan Todi, Biswajit Paria et al.
description: Language-model agents that run long tasks often redo work they have already done: they re-issue a tool call they made earlier and get back exactly the same observation, a step that adds no new information. summary: Language-model agents that run long tasks often redo work they have already done: they re-issue a tool call they made earlier and get back exactly the same observation, a step that adds no new information. Loops appear natively in Qwen, Llama, and Gemini agents and become far more common once the agent's history is compressed to fit its context window.
takeaways: Loops appear natively in Qwen, Llama, and Gemini agents and become far more common once the agent's history is compressed to fit its context window.
DeLoop builds on a simple observation: the agent's own rollout can provide the supervision needed to learn from its loops.
DeLoop learns from these pairs through direct preference optimization and does not require task rewards, gold answers, or LLM judges.
